name: Primal Scream
label: Creation Records
lede: Bobby Gillespie quit the drum stool in the Jesus and Mary Chain to keep a jangly Glasgow band going, then handed one of its songs to a rave DJ who was told to destroy it. Four decades on, the band is still on stage, still picking fights.

eras.title: Dustbin lids in Glasgow
eras.text: Bobby Gillespie grew up in Springburn and Mount Florida, played in a teenage punk band with Alan McGee, and started Primal Scream as a noise project with Jim Beattie. When McGee started Creation Records, the band was there, and so was Gillespie, drumming standing up for The Jesus and Mary Chain.

years.h: Primal Scream starts as a fuzz guitar and two dustbin lids
years.p: Gillespie and Jim Beattie name the band after primal therapy. The first tapes are Gillespie banging bin lids together while Beattie plays fuzz guitar.
years.xp: Gillespie already had a band behind him: in 1978 he, [[Alan McGee|ffacc13a-01e5-4b5d-a455-6a7f302ac9ce]] and a 15-year-old [[Andrew Innes|213b0443-e41c-40d7-b8c2-0bcb4f2b6e57]] formed the Drains, a Glasgow punk group. Innes and McGee later moved to London; Gillespie stayed home.

years.h: The first session, for McGee's Essential label, goes up in smoke
years.p: The band records 'The Orchard', with Judith Boyle singing, for McGee. Beattie has said they burned the master tape.

years.h: Gillespie plays a snare and a floor tom, standing up
years.p: Drumming for [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]], Gillespie copies [[Moe Tucker|66742cdb-d1c2-4546-8204-3ff36db12da9]]'s two-drum stand-up kit and plays on Psychocandy.

years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream discography · Wikipedia: Bobby Gillespie
years.h: 'All Fall Down' is the band's first Creation single
years.p: McGee's label puts out Primal Scream's debut 7-inch, backed with 'It Happens'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream · Wikipedia: Bobby Gillespie
years.h: The Reid brothers make Gillespie pick a band
years.p: William and Jim Reid tell him to fold Primal Scream or leave the Mary Chain. He leaves the Mary Chain.

years.h: A B-side called 'Velocity Girl' lands on C86
years.p: The flip of 'Crystal Crescent' goes on the NME's C86 tape and ties the band to a jangle-pop scene it was keen to get out of.
years.xp: Gillespie wasn't happy with the band on the road that year either. "There was always something missing, musically or in attitude," he said of the 1986 shows.

eras.title: A £100,000 false start
eras.text: A Warner subsidiary paid for the debut, and the debut sank. The band that survived moved to Brighton, put Robert Young on guitar, and started going to raves because McGee wouldn't shut up about them.

years.src: Wikipedia: Sonic Flower Groove · Wikipedia: Primal Scream
years.h: Sonic Flower Groove costs £100,000 and reaches No. 62
years.p: On Warner's Elevation label, sessions with [[Stephen Street|47c7deb5-2e24-45ec-944e-d9d103afb312]] at Rockfield stall; [[Mayo Thompson|b463f760-e381-462a-b060-78606b78e5e1]] of Red Krayola produces the redo. Melody Maker calls most of it "dandelion fluff", and Beattie and Skinner quit.
years.xp: Innes had rejoined on guitar for the album and Gavin Skinner had taken over the drums. Wikipedia puts the cost at £100,000; AllMusic later called it "pristine but dull."

years.cap: Primal Scream on stage in the West Midlands
years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream · Wikipedia: Robert Young
years.h: Brighton, a new rhythm section, and Throb on guitar
years.p: Gillespie, Innes and Young regroup on the coast. Young moves from bass to guitar, and bassist Henry Olsen and drummer Toby Tomanov come in from Nico's band, the Faction.

years.h: McGee takes the band to acid house parties
years.p: Gillespie was curious and unconvinced at first. Within months the band are regulars at raves.
years.xp: "I always remember being quite fascinated by it but not quite getting it," Gillespie said. At one party they met [[Andrew Weatherall|4f4fd405-6ede-4da0-9b74-c422d8e09bed]], who had already written up their second album kindly in the Boys Own fanzine.

years.cap: Primal Scream on stage in the West Midlands, probably Walsall, c. 1989
years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream discography · Wikipedia: Loaded
years.h: The band returns to Creation with a guitar record
years.p: The second album, Primal Scream, comes out on McGee's label. One ballad on it, 'I'm Losing More Than I'll Ever Have', is about to change everything.
play: I'm Losing More Than I'll Ever Have

years.h: With Felt over, Martin Duffy joins full time
years.p: [[Martin Duffy|00d21293-62c1-4c43-a394-b8fd9fa49853]] had already played keys on both albums. With [[Felt|6999f790-25f4-44a3-b745-1e3e01fde0f5]] finished, he's a permanent member.

eras.title: Loaded, then the first Mercury
eras.text: One remix turned a guitar band into the sound of the second summer of love. Andrew Weatherall, who had never produced a record, ended up steering most of Screamadelica, and the album won a brand-new prize ahead of Gillespie's old band.

years.h: Weatherall's first 'Loaded' remix is sent back
years.p: Innes's brief for the second try, per Weatherall. 'Loaded' reaches No. 16, gets the band onto Top of the Pops, and 'Come Together' follows it to No. 26.
years.xp:
The fee was £500. Weatherall's first pass, by his own account, had just "slung a kick drum under the original." The second kept almost nothing of it.

In went Peter Fonda's speech from the biker film The Wild Angels, a vocal from the Emotions, a drum loop lifted from an Italian bootleg remix of Edie Brickell's 'What I Am', and Gillespie singing a line of Robert Johnson. It had more than 7,500 advance orders, almost all from clubs.

years.h: Screamadelica's sun began as a stain on Creation's ceiling
years.p: Paul Cannell painted the cover from a water mark he saw on the office ceiling while on LSD. Inside: Weatherall, the Orb, and the Rolling Stones' producer Jimmy Miller.
years.xp:
[[The Orb|42c14c80-bd17-47e4-9bb2-a35897638c4d]]'s Alex Paterson worked on 'Higher Than the Sun' and [[Jah Wobble|904cc1c8-021e-45ac-bbe9-95c01a1f8099]] played bass on it. "If I died tomorrow, it could be my epitaph," Gillespie told Record Collector. [[Denise Johnson|105235af-71d6-4ea6-a141-f92d0ac6ae09]], a Manchester singer, takes the lead on 'Don't Fight It, Feel It'.

Miller produced 'Movin' On Up' and 'Damaged'. The album reached No. 8. "I honestly thought it would be an underground record like Can's Tago Mago," Gillespie said.

years.cap: Denise Johnson singing with Primal Scream at Club Citta, Kawasaki, Japan
years.h: Glastonbury with the Orb, on a tour famous for its intake
years.p: The Screamadelica tour starts in Amsterdam and ends in Sheffield. Wikipedia says the band and its entourage became known for how much they took.

years.cap: Bobby Gillespie at Club Citta, Kawasaki, Japan
years.h: Screamadelica wins the first Mercury Prize, and the cheque goes missing
years.p: The new award goes to Primal Scream ahead of [[The Jesus and Mary Chain|e938a15c-b17e-4e7a-9f68-ff0d536cab44]]. Record Collector says the band famously lost the cheque.

eras.title: Memphis, and nearly the end
eras.text: The follow-up went to the American South, came back sounding like the Stones, and split the critics. The band's own manager said a US tour nearly finished them, and it took a bassist from The Stone Roses to put them back together.

years.h: Give Out But Don't Give Up splits the room
years.p: 'Rocks' goes to No. 7 in March, the band's biggest hit yet. Some critics liked the Stones swagger of the album, others called it secondhand.
years.xp: Work started at Roundhouse Studios in London in September 1992. The follow-up singles 'Jailbird' and '(I'm Gonna) Cry Myself Blind' each charted lower than the last.
play: Give Out But Don't Give Up

years.h: Touring the US with Depeche Mode nearly breaks the band
years.p: Manager Alex Nightingale called it "the closest we've come to the band splitting up."

years.h: A football single with Irvine Welsh starts a row in Glasgow
years.p: 'The Big Man and the Scream Team Meet the Barmy Army Uptown', made with [[Irvine Welsh|8040b0ce-9257-4e2f-854d-f44bbb56eda4]] and On-U Sound, draws complaints over its words about Rangers and their fans.

years.h: Mani walks from the Stone Roses into the Scream
years.p: With [[The Stone Roses|b5fa29f1-6c22-4321-a488-b5f363b06b06]] gone, [[Gary Mounfield|5d58f893-5734-4229-9580-f068e623d843]] takes the bass. He said Primal Scream were one of only three bands he'd join, with the Mary Chain and [[Oasis|39ab1aed-75e0-4140-bd47-540276886b60]].
years.xp: Wikipedia credits his arrival with talking the band out of splitting. Paul Mulreany came in on drums, and the band made the next record in its own studio over two months, with Innes engineering.

eras.title: Speedfreak road movies and a war on everything
eras.text: Vanishing Point and XTRMNTR are the band at its darkest and loudest, with Kevin Shields of My Bloody Valentine as a near-member. By 2005 Gillespie was getting pulled off stages.

q: An anarcho-syndicalist speedfreak road movie record!
years.h: Vanishing Point is named after a 1971 car-chase film
years.p: 'Kowalski' goes to No. 8 in May. Gillespie's pitch for the album sits in the More.
years.xp: The title track had already been on the Trainspotting soundtrack. [[Brendan Lynch|1aa1cfaa-9f3b-46f4-aa7b-64bde5944c99]] and Weatherall produced. [[Asian Dub Foundation|db612997-f11e-424d-8b41-cf410a433656]] opened the tour and broke through on it.

years.h: "It's not a drugs thing and it's not a nervous breakdown"
years.p: The band's press agent explains away postponed tour dates. Drummer Paul Mulreany leaves, a drum machine fills in, then [[Darrin Mooney|96fde896-9a51-494e-9e59-0a0f046f8bfc]] gets the job.

years.h: XTRMNTR goes to No. 3, with Bernard Sumner on board
years.p: The band, mostly off drugs now, makes its angriest record, with the Chemical Brothers, [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]]'s [[Bernard Sumner|6fa2e161-200e-475a-8492-3755594581f9]] and Shields. NME later put it third among the albums of the decade.
years.xp:
Gillespie said 'Swastika Eyes' was about "American international terrorism", and the single drew complaints on release in November 1999. He wanted the album to say "what it's like to be in Britain in this day and age."

The Shields connection started in February 1998, when he remixed the title track of the If They Move, Kill 'Em EP and then joined the band on tour.

years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream · Wikipedia: Primal Scream discography
years.h: 'Bomb the Pentagon' becomes 'Rise', and Kate Moss sings
years.p: After September 11 the band retitles the song. Evil Heat also has Kate Moss's singing debut on 'Some Velvet Morning' and Robert Plant.

years.h: Glastonbury pulls the plug on an overrunning set
years.p: Gillespie needles the crowd and the band is forced off for running long. Organizers were already angry that he'd changed a 'Make Poverty History' poster to 'Make Israel History'.

eras.title: Country Girl, and Throb's exit
eras.text: The band had its highest-charting single, then lost the guitarist who had been there since the Glasgow days. A 2010 run of full Screamadelica shows turned the old album into a live event.

years.h: 'Country Girl' hits No. 5, the band's highest ever
years.p: Riot City Blues follows it to No. 5 too. The BBC used the single over its 2007 Grand National credits.

years.src: Wikipedia: Robert Young · Wikipedia: Primal Scream
years.h: Robert Young takes a break and doesn't come back
years.p: Young misses the November tour. Gillespie said it was to deal with "problems in his personal life"; [[Barrie Cadogan|546be382-5079-46cf-a997-1ec119e94f1c]] of Little Barrie covers guitar.

years.h: Screamadelica live at Olympia, gospel choir and horns
years.p: Two London nights playing the whole album, the first broadcast on BBC 6 Music. A UK tour of it followed in March 2011.

years.cap: Primal Scream playing Screamadelica live at the Paradiso, Amsterdam, September 2011
years.h: Mani's last Scream show is Edinburgh's Hogmanay
years.p: He goes back to the reformed Stone Roses. [[Debbie Googe|b482bb51-0019-4cbb-ba2a-77fa61211d27]] covers for summer 2012, and Simone Butler takes the bass that October.
years.xp: On June 29, 2012, Primal Scream opened for the Stone Roses at Heaton Park in Manchester.

years.h: Robert 'Throb' Young dies in Hove at 49
years.p: No official cause was given. McGee said Young had fought his demons with drugs and alcohol while the others got clean.

eras.title: Lost tapes, two funerals, still loud
eras.text: The Memphis tapes came out, Gillespie wrote his book, and the band sold half its catalogue. Then it lost two of its longest-serving members, and its biggest show in years ended with a police report.

years.cap: Bobby Gillespie at Rock en Conce, Concepción, Chile, March 2018
years.h: The lost Memphis sessions with Tom Dowd come out
years.p: In 1993 the band cut the Give Out songs at Ardent Studios with [[Tom Dowd|44823452-ad02-4854-8929-7753f71e1c09]] and the Muscle Shoals Rhythm Section. The tapes stayed in a drawer for 25 years.

years.h: Gillespie's Tenement Kid runs from Springburn to Screamadelica
years.p: His memoir arrives the same year as Utopian Ashes, his duet album with [[Jehnny Beth|fdac609a-63d0-49b9-823a-daec52a0db97]].

years.src: NME · Wikipedia: Martin Duffy · Wikipedia: Primal Scream
years.h: Martin Duffy dies at 55
years.p: He died in Brighton of a head injury from falls at home. At the inquest his son said Duffy had been paid as a session player for 30 years.
years.xp:
In June 2023 the coroner recorded accidental death: "severe traumatic head injury as the result of multiple falls" and alcohol intoxication. Louie Duffy said his father hadn't been told about the band selling half its catalogue to BMG in 2022, and that he had told Gillespie he was on benefits. The band gave NME no comment.

When he died, the band said "Martin was the most musically talented of all of us."

years.src: Wikipedia: Primal Scream · Wikipedia: Primal Scream discography
years.h: Come Ahead, announced with 'Love Insurrection'
years.p: The twelfth album comes out on BMG. The live band has grown to twelve, with the House Gospel Choir and Fat White Family's Alex White on sax.

years.h: Mani dies at 63, and the band plays his song in Manchester
years.p: He died at home in Heaton Moor of emphysema. Two days later the band dedicated 'I'm Losing More Than I'll Ever Have' to him at the Warehouse Project, Simone Butler's last show.
years.xp: Butler announced she was leaving on January 28, 2026: "I'll always be part of the Scream family."

years.h: The XTRMNTR show at the Roundhouse ends in a police report
years.p: Visuals for 'Swastika Eyes' put swastikas inside Stars of David in the eyes of Benjamin Netanyahu and other leaders. The Community Security Trust reported the band to police.
years.xp:
The Campaign Against Antisemitism called it "absolutely sickening and totally inexcusable." The band said it was "meant to provoke debate, not hate." A week later Trentham Live dropped their August 2026 headline slot.

[[Phil Mossman|3350b4c2-4f6a-4f5e-9ea2-72102ddd0d2e]], once of Weatherall's Sabres of Paradise, played bass that night.
